Axiom: **Bootstrap Requirements rows with Owner=`this-scope-task` become the minimum coherent capability workstreams per `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`.** Derive only layers demanded by the selected requirements: runtime → package manager/dependencies → language/compiler → quality/test tooling → app platform. This is a platform-neutral taxonomy, not a mandatory five-ticket stack; adapter ids bind the concrete platform facts. Each emitted node carries its closed owner kind: infrastructure rows → `infrastructure-flat`; product/library `this-scope-task` rows → `scope-bootstrap`; product/library module work → `module`. No fourth owner exists; interface never owns a task. - Rows with Owner=`external-prereq-scope` → cross-scope dependency edge, not a ticket here. - Rows with Owner=`operator-action` → noted in tracker index as a blocking external prerequisite, not a ticket. - For each selected layer declare `Capability Adapter`, `Provides Capabilities`, and exact `Requires Capabilities`; every requirement reaches exactly one current/upstream provider through the phase/task DAG. - Every package mutation declares `Bootstrap Action: dependency-install`, exact `Provides Packages`, and Target Files containing the adapter manifest plus future/active lockfile. Consumers declare exact `Requires Packages`. Several layers may write the same manifest/lock only when the DAG strictly serializes them; no global single-owner rule exists. - Populate Verification from the Bootstrap Requirements Resolution command. One package probe proves one exact package; do not merge unrelated package probes. - A causally coupled dependency → config → command-smoke workstream is one DAG-connected ordered chain; coherent spec/context boundaries may split it across serialized tickets or phases. Never gate an earlier node on a later artifact. Project-wide wrappers belong to readiness/full audit. Role=`probe` belongs to the unique test phase owning its mapped test file; `Required-by` is traceability, not phase routing. - The authoring and feasibility tool calls own adapter lookup, rule-file evidence, provider uniqueness/order, package materialization, shared-writer serialization, and smoke ownership diagnostics. Apply their exact finding and rerun; do not reconstruct those mechanics in prose. - If Bootstrap Requirements is absent from the spec → abort with `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` (the spec did not pass discovery STEP_7).
